title: The levers of political persuasion with conversational AI
summary: In three large experiments with 76,977 participants, 19 LLMs argued 707 British political positions in dialogue. Persuasiveness was driven mainly by information density, while tailoring to user traits added little, and post-training for persuasion raised effectiveness by up to 50%. The most persuasive models also produced the most inaccurate claims. Caveat: the persuasion effects are measured in survey experiments, and accuracy was tested on a subset of claims.
ai_technology: 19 open and closed LLMs (including GPT-4.5, GPT-4o, Grok-3)
organization: University of Oxford; UK AI Security Institute; London School of Economics; Stanford University; MIT
